The best central control panel for your smart home is simple: take an old iPad, mount it in a prominent place at home, and set up a dedicated task. The "Home Information Panel" app uses the design of the Apple Home app and perfectly addresses this need. Cameras, heating and cooling, lights, local weather and your calendar are all visible at a glance on the same screen.

The HomeKit Weekly series covers smart home accessories, automation tips, and everything related to the Apple smart home framework.

The camera support feature is my personal favourite. You can preview live feeds from up to four Apple Home cameras simultaneously, and upgrading to the premium version removes the limit. There is also a one-tap switch that instantly syncs all views to live streaming. Tap any camera to display it in full screen. If a camera supports two-way audio, this functionality is built in as well.

For home management, you can control up to four thermostats and up to eight switches, such as lights, outlets and fans, grouped by room. It will also fetch a six-day weather forecast for your home location.

The calendar view is a thoughtful design touch, making the app more than just a smart home management tool. It displays a weekly overview of your shared calendar, highlights the next event, and lets you swipe left or right to switch between weeks. You can also set custom text colours for each calendar, which is very handy if you have multiple calendars tracking different sports fixtures.

What can you do with the "Home Information Panel"?

The app automatically enters sleep mode after a period of inactivity, and can be woken by tapping the screen, detecting motion via the front camera, or through a HomeKit motion sensor. It also automatically switches between light and dark mode according to your iPad settings.

The latest version has added a 3D floor plan. You can upload an image of your home layout, and the app will convert it into an overhead view, placing lights, blinds, sensors and door locks as tappable icons at their actual positions within rooms. For example, you can tap a light bulb icon in the living room to turn that light on or off.

Below the floor plan, live thumbnails from entry point and outdoor cameras each have their own live indicators. You can take a quick look at the front door or the back garden without leaving the app's main screen. The right side of the app features quick scene buttons, positioned below a status bar confirming that all your windows and doors are closed.

The weather info card shows the current temperature along with a six-day forecast, and directly below it, individual room temperature cards let you view and manage each thermostat independently. The calendar panel displays a list of upcoming events spanning seven days, with countdown timers for occasions like holidays or birthdays counting down in days, hours, minutes and seconds.

There is now also an iCloud backup configuration feature, making it very convenient to import or export settings if you use the app across multiple iPads.

The app itself is free; upgrading to the premium version (US$9.99 per year) unlocks unlimited cameras and thermostats, as well as the floor plan feature. The developer has also stated that the app does not collect any data whatsoever.

Summary

If you have a spare iPad lying around and you like Apple Home, this is absolutely a great way to put it to good use. Pairing it with a dedicated wall mount makes it even better. The system requires iPadOS 17 or later, along with an existing HomeKit setup. It also works perfectly in portrait mode on an iPhone with a scrollable layout, if you just want to dip your toes in.

The "Home Information Panel" is now available for free on the App Store.
